subject: Re: Invoice INV-2028-042 — tax/withholding and payment path
messages:
From: Marta Silva <marta.silva@novacorp.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: accounts-payable@novacorp.com
Date: 2028-03-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Invoice INV-2028-042 — tax/withholding question

Hi Kimberly,

We received invoice INV-2028-042 (attached) and wanted to confirm tax treatment before we release payment. Per our local rules we may need to withhold 10% for services unless we receive a VAT invoice showing EU VAT or a completed W-9/W-8 for US vendors.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood has an EU VAT registration for this billing entity, or
- If you can provide a W-9 (we are in Portugal) or a VAT/Tax residency attestation so our AP team can make a gross payment?

Also, what payment rails do you accept for NovaCorp — we can do wire, ACH (US/SEPA) or virtual card. AP prefers wire for international vendors but will consider card if remittance is straightforward.

Thanks — we need this clarified today to hit our March 7 cutoff.

Best,
Marta Silva
Senior AP Analyst
NovaCorp

Attachments: INV-2028-042.pdf (PDF, 88 KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Silva <marta.silva@novacorp.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, accounts-payable@novacorp.com
Date: 2028-03-01T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Invoice INV-2028-042 — tax/withholding question

Hi Marta,

Thanks for the heads-up and the quick timeline. Short answers first:
- Redwood (US entity) does not have an EU VAT registration for this billing entity. We can provide a completed W-9 immediately.
- If NovaCorp withholds, we can (in most cases) issue a credit or a corrected invoice after we receive formal tax residency documentation; we typically handle this on a case-by-case basis.

Payment rails: we accept wire (preferred for international), US ACH (for US accounts), and virtual card. If you wire, please use the remittance details below and include INV-2028-042 in the reference so we can reconcile quickly.

Possible options to keep the March 7 cutoff:
- Option A: NovaCorp proceeds with wire net of withholding now; send us a scan of the withholding certificate and we’ll review for possible credit/adjustment.
- Option B: NovaCorp withholds and includes PO/reference; Redwood issues a corrected invoice once we receive tax residency/W-9 (may take 5–7 business days).
- Option C: Pay by virtual card to avoid withholding; card fee will be visible on the remittance (we can absorb up to $25 of card fees — see Ben’s note below).

I attached our W-9 and a simple tax residency attestation form — if you prefer, I can route these to your compliance team directly. For wiring, remit to:

Redwood Inference (redacted bank stub) — please see attached remit stub for bank details.

If you’d like me to confirm the net amount after a hypothetical 10% withholding, tell me the currency and I’ll reply with the net value to expect.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_W9.pdf, redwood_tax_residency_form.pdf, remit_stub_stub.txt

Marta —

We will proceed with the following to keep this moving:
1) Redwood will email a completed W-9 to accounts-payable@novacorp.com in the next 20 minutes (attached to this thread).
2) If NovaCorp withholds 10% at payment, please wire net of withholding to the bank details in the attached remit stub and include INV-2028-042 in the reference. Once we receive the official withholding certificate/confirmation from NovaCorp AP, Redwood will issue a credit for the withheld amount (or a corrected invoice) within 5 business days.
3) If NovaCorp prefers virtual card instead, we can accept that and Redwood will absorb up to $25 in card fees — please include the invoice reference on the card transaction.

Net calculation example (USD invoice of $12,500):
- Gross: $12,500 USD
- 10% withholding: $1,250 USD
- Remit (net): $11,250 USD

Please confirm which path you’ll choose and we’ll watch for the incoming wire. If you send the withholding certificate to this thread, we’ll prioritize the credit.

Thanks for the quick turnaround on timing.
